name: Art D'Égypte
funding: Private firm of Nadine Abdel Ghaffar. Egypt's foreign and tourism ministries and UNESCO sponsor Forever Is Now. Partners: LMD, Suez Canal Bank, BMW (2026); TotalEnergies, Afreximbank (2024).
watch: In October 2026 a petition of 500 to 700 signatories made it drop sculptor Bernar Venet over Israeli ties; artists and galleries withdrew.
why_flagged: Private firm of Nadine Abdel Ghaffar. Egypt's foreign and tourism ministries and UNESCO sponsor Forever Is Now. Partners: LMD, Suez Canal Bank, BMW (2026); TotalEnergies, Afreximbank (2024).
records_note: It posts no reports or accounts; the site shows four logos of ministries and UNESCO, undated, and lists a three-person team but no board.

name: Art Encounters Foundation
funding: Founded 2015 by developer Ovidiu Șandor, who provides the building. The 2025 biennial had main partner Ploom, Japan Tobacco's heated-tobacco brand, plus Banca Transilvania, Catena and Timișoara municipality funding.
watch: Runs the Art Encounters Biennial (2015 to 2025). A museum-standard venue in the former Casa ISHO opens in September 2026 with a Picasso show.
why_flagged: Founded 2015 by developer Ovidiu Șandor, who provides the building. The 2025 biennial had main partner Ploom, Japan Tobacco's heated-tobacco brand, plus Banca Transilvania, Catena and Timișoara municipality funding.
records_note: It posts no reports, accounts or funder list, only a count of 50 partners; the team page names the president but no board.

name: Art Gallery of Alberta
funding: Revenue C$6.3M in 2023, 46% government. Capital Power has been lead sponsor since 2010 and renewed in January 2023 with the Capital Power Indigenous Art Fund.
watch: Civic art museum in Edmonton. Tri-level public funding provides core stability; corporate partners (such as regional credit unions) are subject to public municipal gift guidelines.
why_flagged: Revenue C$6.3M in 2023, 46% government. Capital Power has been lead sponsor since 2010 and renewed in January 2023 with the Capital Power Indigenous Art Fund.
records_note: It posts yearly reports for 2020 to 2025 that name 2025 donors, lists its board, and files with Canada's charity regulator.

name: Art Gallery of Greater Victoria
funding: Revenue c. CAD 6.1M in 2025 (charity filing via Wikidata); BC, City of Victoria, members, AGGV Foundation endowment.
why_flagged: Name to know: TD Bank pleaded guilty in October 2024 to US money-laundering conspiracy and Bank Secrecy Act failures, paying about $3B. Earned and contributed income supplies the other 60 percent. The March 2026 sponsor page lists local firms and TD; no excluded sponsor.
records_note: Its site blocks automated access with a bot check; search listings show an annual report archive, a 2024-25 financial report and a named board page.

name: Art Gallery of Hamilton
funding: C$7.8M revenue, 177,202 visitors (2024); Canada Council, Ontario Arts Council, City of Hamilton, incite Foundation, BMO, TD, RBC, LiUNA, Peller Estates, CHCH.
watch: Banks (BMO, TD, RBC), union LiUNA, security firm Garda World, winery Peller Estates and Effort Trust are on the roster; none is under campaign.
why_flagged: Name to know: TD Bank pleaded guilty in October 2024 to US money-laundering conspiracy and Bank Secrecy Act failures, paying about $3B. Banks (BMO, TD, RBC), union LiUNA, security firm Garda World, winery Peller Estates, Effort Trust on roster; none under campaign.
records_note: Posts 14 annual reports from 2011 to 2024 with a donor list and a named board, but only a summary of revenue and expenses.

name: Art Gallery of South Australia
watch: BHP principal partner; Samarco dam disaster.
why_flagged: BHP principal partner; Samarco dam disaster.
records_note: Posts annual reports from 2002-03 to 2024-25 with audited statements and names its board; the Tarnanthi page names BHP and the state government.

name: Art Institute of Chicago
watch: Crown family and Griffin money; 68 arrests at a 2024 encampment.
why_flagged: Crown family and Griffin money; 68 arrests at a 2024 encampment.
records_note: It posts annual reports from 2003 to 2024 and its Form 990, names supporters undated, and lists its trustees.

name: Art Macao
records_note: Art Macao is run by the Cultural Affairs Bureau, which names six casino operators as co-organisers for 2025 but publishes no report, accounts or board.

name: Art Tower Mito
funding: Mito City endowed the Mito Arts Foundation with ¥100M and made it manager. 2026 supporters include Suntory, NEC, Joyo Bank, Genden Fureai Ibaraki Foundation and petroleum retailer Yoshida Sekiyu.
watch: Yoshida Sekiyu sells petroleum products and runs ENEOS stations in Ibaraki. Searches found no censorship or protest at Art Tower Mito.
why_flagged: Mito City endowed the Mito Arts Foundation with ¥100M and made it manager. 2026 supporters include Suntory, NEC, Joyo Bank, Genden Fureai Ibaraki Foundation and petroleum retailer Yoshida Sekiyu.
records_note: The foundation posts business reports and accounts for 2012 to 2024, shows 22 supporters as undated logos, and lists no directors.

name: Arter
watch: Koç Holding owns Tüpraş (oil refining) and Otokar (military vehicles).
why_flagged: Koç Holding owns Tüpraş (oil refining) and Otokar (military vehicles).
records_note: Arter has none of its own; parent Vehbi Koç Foundation posts reports for 2012 to 2025 without audited accounts. Arter names sponsors, lists its board.

name: Artists Space
funding: NYSCA and NYC Cultural Affairs; Lambent, Mellon, Goldsmith, Keith Haring, Frankenthaler and Niarchos foundations. Core contributors include the I.A. O'Shaughnessy Foundation, named for oilman Ignatius O'Shaughnessy.
watch: Tribeca alternative space founded in 1972, known for artist advocacy and institutional critique. It operates with complete transparency and rejects corporate board influence.
why_flagged: NYSCA and NYC Cultural Affairs; Lambent, Mellon, Goldsmith, Keith Haring, Frankenthaler and Niarchos foundations. Core contributors include the I.A. O'Shaughnessy Foundation, named for oilman Ignatius O'Shaughnessy.
records_note: Names core contributors and campaign donors with no date and lists its board; no annual report posted, Form 990s for 2001 to 2025 on ProPublica.

name: Arts AlUla and Desert X AlUla
funding: Arts AlUla sits inside the Royal Commission for AlUla, a Saudi government agency overseen by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. US nonprofit Desert Biennial produces Desert X AlUla with it.
watch: Three Desert X board members resigned in October 2019, citing Saudi human rights abuses and the Khashoggi killing. MaddocksBrown Foundation, a donor, withdrew its support.
why_flagged: Arts AlUla sits inside the Royal Commission for AlUla, a Saudi government agency overseen by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. US nonprofit Desert Biennial produces Desert X AlUla with it.
records_note: Arts AlUla posts nothing; the Royal Commission has 2023 and 2024 annual reports, and Desert Biennial files Form 990s, names donors and lists a board.
